serialFormats.description: Bard (June 1980 to present): 3 digits, a letter, then the serial digits; the two digits immediately after the letter (positions 5-6) are the year of manufacture (98 = 1998). Month/week not encoded.
sources: Building Intelligence Center - Bard HVAC age (building-center.org/bard-hvac-age/)
InspectApedia - Bard HVAC & Heater Age (inspectapedia.com/heat/Bard-Heater-Age-Manuals-Contact.php)
howtolookatahouse.com - How can I tell the age of a Bard heat pump from the serial number (2018)
Bard 'Coffee with Cliff' - New serial plate design (bardhvac.com, 2025)
notes: Three independent secondary decoders agree on the rule; not confirmed against a Bard warranty lookup, so confidence is capped at medium.
Examples are constructed to the published rule (year = digits 5-6); they were not taken from dated nameplate photos.
Pre-June-1980 Bard serials (6 digits + 2 letters, second letter = year, B = 1962) and the Apr-May 1980 11-character style are not decoded here; use the data plate date.

Since 2025 Bard prints the serial information as three separate fields on the data plate instead of one string - the year digits are still the two digits after the letter. A date printed on the plate always outranks this decode.

Some Bard serials carry a hyphenated 1-2 digit suffix (e.g. 000F950926066-1 = 1995, the worked example published by building-center.org and the intrysys Bard decoder); the suffix is ignored for dating.

serialFormats.description: Nordyne / Nortek Global HVAC (Intertherm, Miller, Maytag, Frigidaire, Westinghouse, Gibson, Tappan, Kelvinator, Broan, NuTone): 3-letter prefix, then YY (positions 4-5) and MM (positions 6-7), then 5 digits.
sources: Building Intelligence Center - NORDYNE HVAC age (building-center.org/nordyne-hvac-age/)
hvacdecoder.com - Nordyne Serial Number Decoder
howtolookatahouse.com - How can I tell the age of a Nordyne air conditioner from the serial number (2018) - worked example GSD020700023 = July 2002
notes: GSD020700023 = July 2002 is the worked example published by the secondary decoders; the other examples are constructed to the same rule.

Collision: the older Nordyne style puts MM before YY in the same positions (see nordyne-mmyy). When both the YYMM and MMYY readings give a valid month, the era filter decides: MMYY is only used for pre-2000 units. Confirm with the refrigerant on the plate (R-22 = older) and the compressor date code.
Reznor units built after the Nortek acquisition still use the Reznor letter date code, not this format.

serialFormats.description: Older Nordyne style (short transition period ~1997-1999): 3-letter prefix, then MM (positions 4-5) and YY (positions 6-7), then 5 digits - month and year swapped relative to the current style.
sources: Building Intelligence Center - NORDYNE HVAC age (building-center.org/nordyne-hvac-age/)
hvacchecker.com - Nordyne HVAC Age Lookup Tool (mentions month-then-year ordering on older units)
notes: Nordyne 1980-1997 serials encode the year in the FIRST LETTER of the serial (A = 1980 ... M = 1991 ... S = 1997, per building-center.org/nordyne-hvac-age and hvacdecoder.com); this MMYY reading only applies to the short transition period before the YYMM style (~2000). Era narrowed to 1997-1999 so the letter-year scheme is not mis-read as month/year.

LOW confidence: only one secondary source describes the swapped order (units 'older than 12 years' as of ~2010-2012, i.e. roughly pre-1998/2000) and its wording is ambiguous about the cutover year. Treat any pre-2000 Nordyne date as an estimate and confirm from the compressor date code.
Examples are constructed to the rule, not taken from dated plates.
Same regex as nordyne-yymm; the decoder separates them by era and by month validity (a value > 12 in positions 4-5 cannot be a month, so it must be the year).

L = Dec) - followed by the plant code (e.g. 3062 = Monterrey) and a consecutive number.
sources: Reznor Form P-UD 'First Element of the Serial Number - Date of Manufacture' (Reznor date code chart 2002-2020 / 2021-2022 supplement, hosted at jjmorgan.com)

notes: 2021 (BU) and 2022 (BV) were read from the Reznor chart summary; 2023-2028 (BW-CB) are listed in Table 2 of Reznor parts form 1034346-H (08-22). The month letters A-L run January-December (BUA = Jan 2021, BVC = Mar 2022, BXA = Jan 2024 per the same form).

The plant code separator and the consecutive-number length are not documented in the sources; the regex tolerates optional spaces/hyphens. Reznor's online serial lookup (reznorheaters.com) is authoritative.
Examples are constructed from the published month/year letters, not from dated nameplate photos.
Examples are constructed from the published month/year letters; BXA306200001 follows the form's BXA = Jan 2024 entry with the Monterrey plant code.

serialFormats.description: Reznor letter date code for 2015-2020, assuming the second year letter advances one letter per year (BO = 2015 ... BT = 2020). NOT confirmed - use Reznor's serial lookup. 2021-2028 are documented in reznor-letter-2021-2028.
sources: Extrapolated backwards from the Reznor date codes BU = 2021 ... CB = 2028 (parts form 1034346-H); the Reznor Form P-UD chart 2002-2020 summary (jjmorgan.com) is internally inconsistent about 2019/2020 (shows both BS* and BT* under 2020), so BO-BT remain unconfirmed

Reznor's own worked serial in parts form 1034346-0 (03-21) is 'BOG 3062 00000' (date code BOG, plant 3062, consecutive number) - its year is not stated in the form, so it is not used as a dated example.
Pre-2015 Reznor units use earlier letter codes documented in the 'Reznor Date Code 1949-2015' chart - not decoded here.

serialFormats.description: Mitsubishi Electric (M-, P-series, City Multi, US/JP built): first character = last digit of the manufacturing year, second character = month (1-9, X = Oct, Y = Nov, Z = Dec), then the sequence number. Decade candidate 2010-2019.
sources: Building Intelligence Center - Mitsubishi HVAC age (building-center.org/mitsubishi-hvac-age/)
hvacagelookup.com - Mitsubishi HVAC Age Serial Number Decoder
hvacchecker.com - Mitsubishi HVAC Age Lookup Tool

Mitsubishi's production fiscal year starts in April: units built January-March may carry the previous year's digit while the plate build date shows the actual year.

sources: Friedrich PTAC parts manual - 'PTAC Serial Number Identification Guide' (ManualsLib, Friedrich WallMaster WMPTAC02 parts manual p.3; H)A09K25**G parts manual p.2; ZoneAire Select service manual): year code 17-22 (24-29 in current manuals), MONTH code 01-12

notes: Positions assumed plant letter(s) + YY + MM; the Friedrich guide confirms month (01-12), so secondary decoders that call the last two digits a week are superseded. The exact character positions were still not read directly, so confidence stays LOW - confirm against the serial-number guide in the unit's parts manual.
Year codes 17-22 are in the older guides and 24-29 in current Friedrich manuals; the two-digit year is read directly (pivot 70).
Examples are constructed, not from dated plates.

H = 8, J = 9, K = 0; read as 2009-2017 in this era) and a one-letter month code (A = Jan ... H = Aug, J = Sep, K = Oct, L = Nov, M = Dec; I skipped), then the sequence.
sources: Friedrich PTAC parts manual - 'PTAC Serial Number Identification Guide' (ManualsLib, Friedrich WallMaster WMPTAC02 parts manual p.3; H)A09K25 parts manual p.2) - single-letter year digit (A = 1 ... H = 8, J = 9, K = 0), month letters A-M skipping I, plant letter first in the newer guide

The first letter is the plant code (any letter). Examples are constructed from the published letter tables (AKC = plant A, year 0 -> 2010, March; LJM = plant L, year 9 -> 2009, December).
The position of the codes within the serial was not read directly from the guide; verify against the guide printed in the parts manual for the model.

faultCodes.meaning: System lockout - failed to detect or sustain flame
likelyCauses: Spark gap or cracked electrode, shorted spark cable
Dirty or mis-positioned flame sensor / burner not grounded
Gas valve not opening (loose wiring, board not powering valve)
checks: Inlet gas pressure at valve during trial (NG ~5-7 in. w.c., verify plate)
Spark at igniter; spark gap per IOM
Flame current with a microamp meter; clean sensor rod
24 VAC at gas valve terminals during trial for ignition

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure switch did not close within 30 seconds of venter motor being energized
likelyCauses: Venter (inducer) motor not running or slow
Blocked vent / flue or blocked combustion air
Pressure switch tubing cracked or full of water
checks: Venter motor runs on call for heat (check 115 V at motor)
Draft pressure at the switch tap vs. the switch setpoint stamped on the switch
Vent for restriction, ice, bird screen blockage
faultCodes.source: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM (Form I-UDA), DSI control LED table

faultCodes.meaning: High limit or flame rollout switch open
likelyCauses: Low airflow across heat exchanger (fan motor, dirty fan, blocked discharge louvers)
Flame rollout from cracked/blocked heat exchanger or delayed ignition
checks: Fan runs when burner is on; fan control / motor amps
Manifold pressure vs. rating plate
Reset the manual rollout switch only after finding the cause; inspect heat exchanger
faultCodes.source: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM (Form I-UDA), DSI control LED table

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure switch is closed before venter motor is energized
checks: With no call for heat, confirm switch contacts are open (ohm across the switch)
Replace the switch if welded closed
faultCodes.source: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM (Form I-UDA), DSI control LED table

faultCodes.meaning: Blown fuse, no power, or defective board
checks: Check the board fuse
24 VAC at the control transformer secondary and at the board
faultCodes.source: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM (Form I-UDA), DSI control LED table

ledPatterns.meaning: No power / blown fuse / failed board

diagnosticTips: The LED is on the integrated ignition control inside the control compartment (remove the side access panel).

A 1-flash (soft) lockout is reset by removing power from the control for more than one second, or by removing the thermostat call for heat for more than 1 second and LESS than 20 seconds (Form I-UDA p.25); the control retries ignition trials before locking out. A hard lockout (board fault, LED off) self-resets only when the hardware fault clears.

Ignition-failure causes listed in the IOM: loose wiring, transformer failure, incorrect spark gap, shorted spark cable/electrode, burner or board not grounded, blown board fuse, faulty board, lockout device open, faulty combustion-air proving switch, main valve not operating.

controls.name: Mitsubishi Electric City Multi / P-series check codes (M-NET, 4-digit)
controls.description: 4-digit check codes displayed on the outdoor unit LED/7-segment display, the wired remote controller (PAR-xx), the MA/ME controllers and centralized controllers (AE-200/EW-50). Codes are shared across City Multi VRF and (largely) P-series splits; the P-series/Mr. Slim A-control 2-character codes (P/E/F/U) are included. Coverage is partial (97 codes transcribed): preliminary codes (12xx, 14xx, 15xx sub-codes), 2000-series water-side codes for PQHY/PQRY/PWFY, 3121/3152, several 41xx/42xx/51xx/6xxx/71xx codes and the inverter detail codes (101-137) are omitted - see the outdoor unit Service Handbook check code list. Thermistor attribution for 5101-5107 differs between indoor and outdoor units and between outdoor unit generations (older lists show 5104 as outside temperature; PUHY/PURY HP/YLM handbooks show 5104 = TH4 discharge, 5107 = TH7 outside) - always read the attribute/address shown with the code and use the thermistor table for that unit.

faultCodes.meaning: Discharge temperature fault (abnormal discharge temperature, TH4)
likelyCauses: Indoor or outdoor LEV not opening (stuck, coil or connector fault)
Refrigerant service valve not fully open
Discharge thermistor TH4 reading high (drift, poor contact with pipe)
checks: Per handbook: check refrigerant charge; check operating conditions and operation status of indoor/outdoor units; check indoor/outdoor LEV (see 1202 preliminary code) and confirm the refrigerant service valve is fully open
Compare TH4 on the maintenance monitor with a clamp thermistor on the discharge line (field practice)
Discharge superheat and system subcooling versus the service handbook charge tables
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (1102 'Discharge temperature fault'); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186); Logicool City Multi Codes.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: High pressure fault (abnormal high pressure; 63H high-pressure switch operated or 63HS above the limit; on the second stop of the outdoor unit for high pressure the outdoor unit makes an error stop and 1302 is displayed)
likelyCauses: Outdoor fan not running / fan inverter fault (cooling)
Dirty or blocked outdoor coil, short-circuited discharge air
Indoor airflow restriction in heating (filters, closed dampers)
63HS high-pressure sensor or 63H switch / wiring fault
checks: Per handbook: check the fan on the outdoor unit; check the high-pressure sensor 63HS and the 63H switch connector
Actual head pressure at the gauge versus the 63HS value on the maintenance monitor
Verify all service valves fully open and the outdoor coil clean (field practice)
Reset by cycling power at the outdoor unit after the cause is corrected
faultCodes.source: PUHY-P200 Service Handbook, Error Code [1302] (During operation) (p.182); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (1302 'High pressure fault - check the fan on the outdoor unit')

faultCodes.meaning: Reverse phase / open phase detection (abnormal phase sequence of the three-phase supply)
likelyCauses: Two power legs swapped at the outdoor unit terminal block
Lost phase / blown fuse on one leg
checks: Phase rotation at L1/L2/L3 with a rotation meter; swap two legs at the outdoor terminal block only (field practice)
Voltage on all three phases at the terminal block, imbalance under 2%
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4103 'Reverse phase / open phase'); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186)

faultCodes.meaning: Power supply signal sync error (power synchronization / input circuit (board) failure - electrical system cannot operate because of the power supply)
likelyCauses: Input circuit on the outdoor control board failed
checks: Per handbook [4115]: check the power supply voltage/frequency; if normal, replace the control board (input circuit failure)
Check ground and shielding of power and transmission wiring (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-P200YLM-A(1) Service Handbook, Error Code [4115] (p.252); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4115 'Power supply signal sync error')

faultCodes.meaning: No ACK error (no acknowledgement returned from the addressed unit on the M-NET transmission line while the system is operating; error source address and attribute (OC/IC/BC/Lc/RC) are displayed with the code)
likelyCauses: Transmission wiring (M1/M2) open, shorted or poor terminal on the unit named
Unit powered down or its address changed
Transmission booster / M-NET power supply failed
checks: Per handbook [6607] (by error source address): check power and transmission wiring to the unit named; check its address switch; confirm the transmission booster is powered
M-NET DC bus voltage at TB3/TB7 (about 24-30 VDC) and continuity/polarity of the shielded 2-wire line (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Code [6607] Error source address = Lossnay (Lc) (p.240) and adjoining [6607] pages; CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (6607 'No ACK error')

faultCodes.meaning: Serial communication error (between the outdoor control board and the INV board / fan board)
likelyCauses: Loose or unplugged board-to-board connectors (control board CN4A/CN4B, fan board CN80)
INV board or fan board failure
Noise on the internal serial link
checks: Per handbook: check control board (CN4A, CN4B) and fan board (CN80) connections; if the problem recurs replace the INV board or fan board
Cycle power at the outdoor unit and watch for the code to return (field practice)
Read the error detail code on the outdoor LED display to identify which board dropped the link
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Code Definitions and Solutions: Codes [0-999], Error Code [0403] (p.190); PUHY-P200 Service Handbook [0403] (p.178)

faultCodes.meaning: Test run (unit in test run / trial operation mode; on Lossnay: test operation dipswitch set ON)
likelyCauses: Lossnay main board test dipswitch SW2-1 left ON
Test run started and not ended
checks: Check the position of dipswitch SW2-1 on the Lossnay main control board; set OFF when test is not required
Not a fault: end the test run from the controller or dipswitch and the indication clears
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (0900 'Test run', attribute LC); Lossnay handbook / arlingtonairconditioningheating decoder (Lossnay test dipswitch SW2-1)

faultCodes.meaning: Low pressure fault (low pressure detected before starting; e.g. low pressure reads 0.098 MPa or less when starting the compressor from stop mode for the first time)
likelyCauses: Closed service valve on the low side
Indoor airflow problems in heating (dirty filter, blocked heat exchanger)
checks: Per handbook: inspect thermistors TH2, TH3, TH4, refrigerant charge, indoor fan, heat exchanger and filters
Compare the 63LS reading on the maintenance monitor with a gauge on the low-side port
Confirm all service valves are fully open (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PUHY-P200 Service Handbook, Error Code [1301] (p.181); PUHY-HP72 Service Handbook [1301] (p.130); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (1301 'Low pressure fault')

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant overcharge (detected from excessive subcooling / discharge superheat)
likelyCauses: System overcharged (wrong additional-charge calculation for piping length)
Thermistor fault giving a false low discharge superheat
checks: Per handbook: check refrigerant charge; check LEV1/LEV2
Recalculate the additional charge from the as-built piping lengths and weigh out refrigerant if over (field practice)
Compare TH4 discharge temperature and 63HS on the maintenance monitor
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (1500 'Refrigerant overcharge - check refrigerant charge, check LEV1/LEV2'); PURY-P72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.204)

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigerant shortage / suction pressure fault (high compressor shell temperature or low suction pressure caused by insufficient refrigerant)
likelyCauses: Insufficient indoor units running (low index) with long piping
Closed or partly closed service valve
LEV stuck closed on the circuit
checks: Per secondary list: check for shortage of gas; check for insufficient indoor index running
Leak search and weigh-in charge to the nameplate plus additional-charge calculation (field practice)
Compare TH15 shell-bottom / TH4 discharge temperature and 63LS suction pressure on the maintenance monitor
faultCodes.source: Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris/mcsprogram mirror: 1501 'High compressor shell temp - check for shortage of gas, insufficient indoor index running'); PURY-P72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.204) lists 1501 next to 1500 (preliminary suction pressure fault); becoolrefrigeration.co.uk list

faultCodes.meaning: Drain sensor submergence (water detected at the drain sensor; leakage or drain pump problem on an indoor unit)
likelyCauses: Blocked condensate drain or drain pan
Failed drain pump or pump not powered
Water leaking from the humidifier or pan onto the sensor
checks: Per source: drain sensor is submerged or the drain pump has failed - check the pump, pan and drain line
Pour water into the pan and confirm the pump runs and the line drains (field practice)
Check drain sensor resistance and connector
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (2500 'Drain sensor submergence'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Drain pump fault (models with a drain sensor or a float switch: the indoor unit detected that water is not leaving the pan / float switch operated)
likelyCauses: Drain pump failed or its connector loose
Blocked drain line or trap, pan overflow
Float switch stuck or wiring open
Drain sensor fault (models with drain sensor)
checks: Per handbook [2502]: check drain pump operation and the drain sensor / float switch wiring and connector
Confirm 230 V (or board output) at the pump connector when the fault is active (field practice)
Clear the drain line, clean the pan, test with water
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Code [2502] (Models with a drain sensor) (p.197) and (Models with a float switch) (p.198); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Drain sensor (Thd) fault (drain sensor thermistor open/short or disconnected)
likelyCauses: Drain sensor disconnected from the indoor board
checks: Check the drain sensor connector on the indoor board and the sensor resistance versus the thermistor table
Replace the drain sensor if open/short; if normal, suspect the indoor board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (2503 'Drain sensor (Thd) fault'); CMB-WP1016V-GA1 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.120)

faultCodes.meaning: Water leakage (water leak from humidifier)
checks: Inspect the humidifier feed, float valve and overflow; dry and reset
faultCodes.source: Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris/mcsprogram mirror: 2600 'water leak from humidifier'); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (2600 'Water leakage')

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor overcurrent protection (overcurrent break / compressor current interruption)
likelyCauses: Loose, disconnected or reversed compressor wiring
checks: Per source: check inverter or compressor; check power supply, stop valves and compressor wiring
Compressor winding resistance and megohm to ground with power off (field practice)
Supply voltage under load on all phases
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4100 'Compressor overcurrent protection'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror: 'Compressor over current protection on Mr Slim with M-net interface - check inverter or compressor'); MrSlimerrorCode.pdf (4100 <UF> compressor current interruption, locked compressor)

faultCodes.meaning: Open phase (loss of phase in the power supply)
likelyCauses: One supply leg lost (blown fuse, loose lug)
Wiring error at the terminal block
checks: Per source: check the power supply and noise filter for loss of phase; check wiring and fuses
Measure all three phase-to-phase voltages at TB1 under load (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris/mcsprogram mirror: 4102 'open phase fault'); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Overcurrent protection (DOL / non-inverter compressor or fan motor overcurrent relay 51C operated)
likelyCauses: Power supply voltage low or phase loss
Compressor mechanically tight or shorted winding
checks: Per source: check power supply, contactor and compressor
Running amps per phase versus nameplate RLA; winding resistance balance (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris/mcsprogram mirror: 4108 'Overcurrent protection on DOL compressor - check power supply, contactor and compressor'); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4108 'Overcurrent protection')

faultCodes.meaning: Fan speed abnormality / motor abnormality (RPM error on an indoor unit or Lossnay fan motor)
likelyCauses: Fan motor failure (indoor unit or Lossnay)
checks: Per source: check the fan motor and the board (indoor unit or Lossnay unit)
Spin the fan by hand for drag; check motor connector and the fan tach/feedback wiring (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-P200YLM-A(1) Service Handbook, Error Code [4116] (p.252); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4116 'RPM error / motor error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter abnormality (VDC sensor / circuit failure on the inverter)
checks: Read the inverter detail code on the outdoor LED display (SW1 setting per handbook)
Check DC bus voltage and the inverter board connectors; replace INV board if it recurs
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4200 'Inverter abnormality'); errorcodeairconditioning.blogspot City Multi list

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor overcurrent interruption (inverter overcurrent break) / failure in the 12 VDC power supply circuit on the power circuit board
checks: Per source: check stop valves, supply voltage, compressor wiring and fan operation
Compressor winding resistance and megohm to ground; inverter output voltage balance (field practice)
faultCodes.source: MrSlimerrorCode.pdf (4210 <UP> 'Compressor overcurrent interruption / failure in 12 VDC power supply circuit'); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4210 'Overcurrent break')

faultCodes.meaning: Abnormal bus voltage drop / bus voltage abnormality (e.g. detail code 108: Vdc 289 V or less detected during inverter operation)
likelyCauses: Power supply voltage low or momentary interruption
Inverter board, noise filter or DC reactor fault
checks: Per handbook: check that the supply voltage (L1-L2, L2-L3, L1-L3) is not 342 V or less on any phase; check inverter board / noise filter / fan board / control board wiring; if the problem recurs replace the INV board
Read the detail code (108 etc.) from the outdoor LED display to identify the sub-fault (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [4220, 4225] Detail Code 108 (p.208); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4220 'Bus voltage abnormality')

faultCodes.meaning: Heatsink overheat protection (inverter radiating thermostat / heat-sink temperature abnormality)
likelyCauses: Heat-sink cooling air passage blocked (dirt, debris)
Outdoor fan or fan inverter board not running
High ambient at the electrical box
checks: Per handbook: check the fan inverter board and outdoor unit fan; ensure the heat-sink cooling air passage is not blocked
Compare THHS on the maintenance monitor with the actual heat-sink temperature (field practice)
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4230 'Heatsink overheat protection'); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186)

faultCodes.meaning: Overload protection (over-current protection: high current detected for more than 10 minutes)
likelyCauses: Compressor running heavy (high head, overcharge, restriction)
checks: Per source: if high current is detected for more than 10 minutes, check inverter balance
Check operating pressures and airflow for the cause of high load (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris/mcsprogram mirror: 4240 'over current protection ... check inverter balance'); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4240 'Overload protection')

faultCodes.meaning: IPM error / power module abnormality / overcurrent protection (the IPM on the inverter detected a short, ground fault, or instantaneous overcurrent; detail codes e.g. [101] IPM error, [102] ACCT overcurrent (H/W detection))
likelyCauses: Shorted or grounded compressor motor winding
Voltage imbalance from the building service
Compressor drawing high amps from mechanical wear
checks: Per handbook: read the detail code; check compressor winding resistance and insulation, the inverter output and the ACCT sensor; replace INV board if the inverter test fails
Measure phase-to-phase supply voltage balance (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [4250, 4255] Detail Code 104 (p.218); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4250 'IPM/bus voltage abnormality / power module abnormality'); mountainmechanicalny.com (corroboration)

faultCodes.meaning: Preliminary inverter heat sink overheat protection (heat-sink overheat protection at startup / fan control)
likelyCauses: Fan inverter board / outdoor fan fault
checks: Per handbook: check the fan inverter board, outdoor unit fan and the heat-sink cooling air passage
See 4230
faultCodes.source: Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris/mcsprogram mirror: 4260 'preliminary inverter heat sink overheat protection'); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Serial communication error (communication lost between control board and inverter / panel)
likelyCauses: INV board or control board failure
checks: Check the connectors between the control board and the INV board; cycle power; replace the board named by the detail code if it recurs (field practice, from the 0403 procedure)
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (4300 'Serial communication error'); errorcodeairconditioning.blogspot City Multi list (4300 'Serial communication error / panel communication error')

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault (thermistor open/short). Indoor unit source: intake (return-air) temperature TH21. Outdoor unit source varies by generation (discharge / suction thermistor) - read the attribute/address shown with the code
likelyCauses: Thermistor open or shorted / harness damage
Indoor or outdoor control board input fault
checks: Per handbook: if a short (high-temperature reading) or open (low-temperature reading) is detected, the unit stops and enters 3-minute anti-restart mode; if detected again after the restart the error stop occurs. Check the thermistor resistance (about 6.4 kOhm at 20 C, 4.3 kOhm at 30 C, 3.1 kOhm at 40 C for the standard element) and the connector contacts
Compare the sensor value on the maintenance monitor with a reference thermometer (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [5101, 5102, 5103, 5104] (p.221); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (5101 'Temperature sensor fault - TH21 intake')

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault (thermistor open/short). Indoor unit source: liquid pipe temperature TH22. Outdoor unit source (PUHY/PURY): HIC bypass circuit outlet temperature TH2
checks: Per handbook: check thermistor resistance against the table and connector contacts; replace the thermistor; if no fault is found the board may be faulty
Unit enters 3-minute anti-restart on first detection; error stop on the second
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [5101, 5102, 5103, 5104] (p.221); PUHY-HP72 Service Handbook [5102...5115] (p.160); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault (thermistor open/short). Indoor unit source: gas pipe temperature TH23. Outdoor unit source (PUHY/PURY): pipe temperature at heat exchanger outlet TH3
checks: Per handbook: check thermistor resistance against the table and the connector on the board; replace if open/short
faultCodes.source: PURY-P200YLM-A(1) Service Handbook, Error Codes [5103...5112] (p.266); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (5103 'gas-side pipe temperature')

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault (thermistor open/short). Outdoor unit source (PUHY/PURY HP/YLM generation): outdoor unit discharge temperature TH4; on older lists 5104 is shown as the outside-air temperature sensor - confirm with the attribute/address displayed
likelyCauses: Discharge thermistor TH4 disconnected, open or shorted
Sensor out of its well / harness chafed on hot pipe
checks: Per handbook: check TH4 resistance and connector; unit enters 3-minute anti-restart on first detection, error stop on recurrence
Verify the sensor is seated in its holder on the discharge line (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [5104, 5105, 5106, 5107, 5109, 5111] (p.222); PUHY-HP72 Service Handbook (p.160); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (5104 'Outside temperature' on older units)

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault - thermistor TH5 open/short (outdoor unit; e.g. accumulator inlet / pipe temperature depending on model)
likelyCauses: TH5 thermistor disconnected, open or shorted
checks: Per handbook: check TH5 resistance versus the thermistor table and its connector on the control board
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [5104, 5105, 5106, 5107, 5109, 5111] (p.222); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror: 5105-5110 'open/short circuit of TH5-TH10')

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault - HIC circuit outlet temperature TH6 (thermistor open/short)
likelyCauses: TH6 thermistor disconnected, open or shorted
checks: Per source: check if the thermistor is disconnected from the board; check resistance versus the table
faultCodes.source: PUHY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [5102...5115] (p.160); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault - outside (ambient) temperature TH7 (thermistor open/short)
likelyCauses: TH7 thermistor disconnected, open or shorted
Harness damage at the coil guard
checks: Per source: check if the thermistor is disconnected from the board; check resistance versus the table and compare with actual ambient
faultCodes.source: PUHY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Codes [5102...5115] (p.160); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature sensor fault - heat-sink temperature THHS (inverter heat-sink thermistor open/short; backup operation possible)
likelyCauses: THHS thermistor on the INV board open/short
checks: Per source: if the problem recurs when the unit is put into operation, replace the INV board
Read the inverter detail code on the outdoor LED display
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (5110 'Temperature sensor fault - heatsink THHS'); snowflakeaircon.sg 5110 page; Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor shell bottom temperature sensor fault (TH15 thermistor open/short)
likelyCauses: TH15 thermistor disconnected, open or shorted
checks: Per handbook: check TH15 resistance versus the table and its connector
faultCodes.source: PUHY-HP72 / PUHY-P250YNW-A Service Handbooks, Error Codes [5102,5103,5104,5105,5106,5107,5115] (p.160 / p.163)

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure sensor fault (high-pressure sensor 63HS open/short or reading out of range)
checks: Compare the 63HS value on the maintenance monitor with a gauge on the high-side port; check the sensor connector and output voltage per the handbook (field practice + handbook)
Swap in a known-good sensor if the reading is implausible
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (5201 'Pressure sensor fault'); Logicool City Multi Codes.pdf; PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186)

faultCodes.meaning: Current sensor / circuit fault (IAC / ACCT sensor or circuit failure; also raised for open-circuited IPM or loose connector wiring; backup operation, detail codes 116/117/120)
likelyCauses: ACCT current sensor open or unplugged
Loose compressor wiring at the inverter
checks: Per handbook: check the inverter error detail code, the resistance of the current sensor and the connections of the sensors
Confirm compressor wiring is tight at the INV board terminals (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Code [5301] Detail Code 116/117 (p.227) and Detail Code 120 (p.230); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (5301 'Current sensor fault'); Logicool City Multi Codes.pdf ('error of circuit, IAC sensor')

faultCodes.meaning: Condensate pan float switch (float switch contact / connector abnormality)
likelyCauses: Float switch stuck or wiring open
checks: Check the float switch connector on the indoor board and switch continuity in both positions (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris/mcsprogram mirror: 5701 'condensate pan float switch'); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Duplex address error (there are 2 units or more with the same address in their controller among outdoor unit, indoor unit, Fresh Master, Lossnay or remote controller)
likelyCauses: Two or more units set to the same M-NET address
Noise interference on indoor/outdoor transmission connectors
checks: Per handbook: find the units with the duplicated address (the code shows the address/attribute), change the address switches and reset the units (power cycle)
Check shield grounding of the transmission line if addresses are correct (noise)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Code [6600] (p.235); PURY-P200YLM-A(1) Service Handbook [6600] (p.276); PUHY-EP250 Service Handbook [6600] (p.190)

faultCodes.meaning: Transmission processor hardware error (a transmitting data collision occurred because wiring work or a polarity change was performed while the power was ON on an indoor/outdoor unit, Fresh Master or Lossnay; or malfunction of the transmitting circuit; or noise on the transmission line)
likelyCauses: Transmission wiring altered with power on
Transmission circuit failure on the unit's board (possibly Lossnay board)
Noise interference on the M-NET line
checks: Per source: check comms wiring; power down all units and restart; if it persists on one address suspect that unit's board (e.g. Lossnay board)
Verify shield is grounded at the outdoor unit only (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186) / [6602] definition as reproduced in search; Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Transmission bus BUSY error (transmission cannot be performed for 4-10 consecutive minutes due to collision of data transmission, or the command cannot be transmitted for 4-10 minutes in a row due to noise)
likelyCauses: Short-cycle voltage such as noise mixed on the transmission line
Increase of transmission data caused by miswiring of TB3 (indoor/outdoor transmission) and TB7 (centralized control) on the outdoor unit
Too many devices / transmission booster missing
checks: Per handbook: check that TB3 on the OC and OS are properly connected and TB3/TB7 are not cross-wired; reset power to the outdoor unit
Measure M-NET DC voltage at TB3/TB7 and check shield grounding (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PEFY-P72NMHSU-E Technical & Service Manual, Transmission line bus busy error (p.38); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (6603 'Transmission bus BUSY error')

faultCodes.meaning: Signal communication error with transmission processor (communication error between the device processor and the transmission processor on the same board)
likelyCauses: Board fault on the unit named by the address
Power supply to the M-NET line unstable
checks: Per source: check M-NET voltage
Power cycle the unit named by the code; if it recurs replace that unit's control board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PEFY-P72NMHSU-E Technical & Service Manual, Communication error between device and transmission processors (p.38); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (6606); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: No response frame error (the addressed unit acknowledged but did not return a response frame within the time limit)
likelyCauses: Transmission line voltage low / booster problem
Board fault on the unit named
checks: Check M-NET voltage and shield grounding; power cycle the affected unit; if repeated on one address suspect its board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (6608 'No response frame error'); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186)

faultCodes.meaning: MA communication receive error (no receive signal) - communication between the MA remote controller and the indoor unit is not done properly
likelyCauses: MA remote controller wiring (A/B) disconnected, shorted or poor contact
More remote controllers or indoor units in the group than allowed
Noise on the remote controller line
Remote controller or indoor board failure
checks: Per handbook [6831]: check the remote controller wiring, the number of controllers/indoor units in the group (limits), the main/sub setting and the power supply to the remote controller (indoor LED2 shows MA line power)
Measure DC voltage on the A/B remote controller terminals (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PURY-HP72 Service Handbook, Error Code [6831] (p.246); PURY-P200YLM-A(1) Service Handbook [6831] (p.287); PUMY-P200YKM Technical & Service Manual 'MA communication receive error' (p.81)

faultCodes.meaning: MA communication send error (synchronous recovery error)
likelyCauses: Remote controller wiring problem or noise
Two MA remote controllers both set as main
checks: Same checks as 6831: wiring, group count, main/sub setting, noise
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (6832 'MA communication send error'); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror: 'synchronous recovery error')

faultCodes.meaning: MA communication send error (H/W error)
likelyCauses: Indoor board MA transmission circuit failure
Short on the remote controller line
checks: Disconnect the remote controller and check the line for shorts; swap the remote controller; if persistent replace the indoor board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (6833 'MA communication send error (H/W error)'); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook Error Code Lists (p.186)

faultCodes.meaning: MA communication receive error (start bit detection error) - MA controller signal reception error
likelyCauses: Noise or poor connection on the MA remote controller line
Remote controller or indoor board failure
checks: Per handbook [6834]: check the remote controller wiring and connections, the wiring length and noise sources; check the main/sub setting
Reseat the A/B terminals at both ends (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PEFY-P72NMHSU-E Technical & Service Manual, Error code 6834 MA controller signal reception error (start bit detection error) (p.51); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook [6834] (p.249)

faultCodes.meaning: Total capacity error (the total capacity of the connected indoor units exceeds the limit for the outdoor unit)
likelyCauses: Too many / too large indoor units connected (over the allowed connection ratio)
Indoor unit capacity code (SW2) set wrong
checks: Per handbook [7100]: check the total capacity of the indoor units against the outdoor unit limit and the capacity code switch settings; correct and reset power
Secondary: PURY (R2) allows up to 150% of outdoor capacity, PUHY/PUMY up to 130%
faultCodes.source: PUHY-P200 Service Handbook, Error Code Definitions and Solutions: Codes [7000-7999], Error Code [7100] (p.235); PURY-HP72 Service Handbook [7100] (p.250); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Capacity code setting error (the model name/capacity code set by the switch differs from the unit connected)
likelyCauses: SW2 capacity code on the indoor unit board set wrong
Outdoor unit model switch (e.g. SW5 on YHM units) set wrong
checks: Per source: check the model name (capacity code) of the indoor unit which has the error source address, set by SW2 on the indoor board; when it differs from the unit connected, turn off power and correct the capacity code
faultCodes.source: PUHY-YMC Installation Manual, How to cope with test run abnormality (p.35); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7101 'Capacity code error')

faultCodes.meaning: Connecting unit number error (the number of units connected to the outdoor terminal block TB3 exceeds the limitation, or units are missing)
likelyCauses: Too many indoor units / BC controllers on TB3
Loss of M-NET voltage so units are not counted
Wiring between OC and OS / BC incorrect
checks: Per source: check whether the number of units connected to the outdoor terminal block (TB3) for indoor/outdoor transmission lines does not exceed the limitation
Check M-NET voltage at TB3 (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PUHY-YMC Installation Manual, How to cope with test run abnormality (p.35); CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7102 'Connecting unit number error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Address setting error (a unit's address is outside the allowed range for its type: OC 51-100, IC 1-50, BC 52-100, RC 101-150 etc.)
likelyCauses: Address switches set outside the valid range
Indoor address higher than allowed, or outdoor address not set +50
checks: Per source: check the address setting on the unit named by the code and set it within the range for that unit type; power cycle
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7105 'Address setting error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror); Logicool City Multi Codes.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Attribute setting error
likelyCauses: Unit attribute (type) setting inconsistent with its address / group
checks: Check the unit's address and attribute settings against the system layout; correct and power cycle
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7106 'Attribute setting error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Port setting error (BC controller port setting incorrect)
likelyCauses: Indoor unit assigned to a BC port that does not match the piping/port setting
checks: Check BC controller port assignments (SW on the indoor unit or BC) against the piping; correct and power cycle
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7107 'Port setting error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Connection information signal transmission/reception error
likelyCauses: Transmission booster powered off (e.g. booster fed from a switched indoor unit circuit)
TB3 on OC and OS not properly connected
Outdoor model selection switch (SW5-7) set wrong
checks: Per source: confirm the transmission booster power is not cut off and the booster is on; confirm TB3 on OC and OS are properly connected; check the model selection switch (SW5-7) on the outdoor control board
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7110 'Connection information signal transmission/reception error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Remote controller sensor fault (the remote controller sensor is selected (SW1-1 ON) but no controller with a sensor is connected, or the remote controller is faulty)
likelyCauses: Indoor SW1-1 set to remote controller sensor with no wired controller / a controller without a sensor
checks: Per source: SW1-1 ON and no controllers fitted, or faulty remote controller - set SW1-1 OFF or connect a controller with a built-in sensor
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7111 'Remote controller sensor fault'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Function setting error (unit function / model-type setting inconsistent; check connector CNTYP on the control board)
likelyCauses: Model type connector CNTYP (e.g. CNTYP5) not connected or wrong
Function setting switches wrong for the unit
checks: Per source: check the connector CNTYP5 on the control board for proper connection; correct function settings and power cycle
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7113 'Function setting error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Model setting error (outdoor unit model setting / model connector inconsistent)
likelyCauses: Model setting connector CNTYP on the control board disconnected or wrong
Replacement control board not set for the unit model
checks: Per source: check the connector CNTYP5 on the control board for proper connection; set the model switches per the handbook after a board replacement
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7117 'Model setting error'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Incompatible unit combination (indoor unit(s) not compatible with the connected outdoor unit / refrigerant type)
likelyCauses: Indoor unit model not compatible with this outdoor unit generation (e.g. R22 indoor on R410A outdoor)
Mixed unit types not allowed on the same system
checks: Check indoor unit models against the outdoor unit's compatibility list in the installation manual; replace or reconfigure the incompatible unit
faultCodes.source: CityMultiErrorCode.pdf (7130 'Incompatible unit combination'); Mitsubishi City Multi Error Code List (baileyharris mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: Abnormality of room temperature thermistor (TH1) - inspected unit: indoor
likelyCauses: TH1 intake thermistor open/short or disconnected
checks: Check TH1 resistance versus the thermistor table and its connector on the indoor board; replace if open/short
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (F/P) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au); MrSlimerrorCode.pdf

faultCodes.meaning: Abnormality of pipe temperature thermistor / liquid (TH2) - inspected unit: indoor
likelyCauses: TH2 liquid pipe thermistor open/short or out of its holder
checks: Check TH2 resistance and connector; confirm the sensor is clipped to the liquid pipe
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (F/P) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au)

faultCodes.meaning: Abnormality of drain sensor (DS) - inspected unit: indoor
checks: Per source: check the drain sensor resistance and connections
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (F/P) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au); acerrorcode.com (corroboration)

faultCodes.meaning: Malfunction of drain-up machine (drain pump fault / high condensate level detected) - inspected unit: indoor
likelyCauses: Drain pump failed or not powered
Blocked drain line, tray or trap
checks: Per source: inspect for blockages in the drain, tray, or possible pump failure
Pour water into the pan and verify the pump runs and drains (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (F/P) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au)

faultCodes.meaning: Freezing/overheating protection detect (indoor coil freeze protection in cooling or overheat protection in heating) - inspected unit: indoor
likelyCauses: Low indoor airflow (dirty filter, fan fault, blocked coil)
checks: Check filter, indoor fan speed and coil; check pipe thermistor TH2/TH5 readings; check charge and superheat/subcooling (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (F/P) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au)

faultCodes.meaning: Abnormality of pipe temperature (pipe temperature not changing as expected - problem with the outdoor/condensing unit, e.g. compressor not running, wrong 4-way valve position, miswired S1/S2/S3) - inspected unit: indoor
likelyCauses: Outdoor unit not running (compressor / inverter fault, open stop valve issue)
Refrigerant leak or pipes crossed between twin/triple units
checks: Per source: P8 indicates a problem with the condensing (outdoor) unit - check the outdoor unit for an error (LED1/LED2), compressor operation and 4-way valve
Confirm pipe temperature changes after start; check thermistor placement (field practice)
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (F/P) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au); justanswer / choosesanford P8 guides (corroboration)

faultCodes.meaning: Abnormality of pipe temperature thermistor / condenser-evaporator (TH5) - inspected unit: indoor
checks: Check TH5 resistance versus the table and its connector on the indoor board
faultCodes.source: Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au); MrSlimerrorCode.pdf; PAR-21MAA Technical Manual (F/P) (p.48)

faultCodes.meaning: Remote controller transmission error (signal receiving error) - inspected unit: remote controller
likelyCauses: Remote controller wiring (A/B) open, shorted or poor contact
Low voltage on the remote controller line
Two controllers both set as main, or wrong master/slave setting in grouped systems
checks: Per source: verify wiring, voltage and connections; if multiple systems are connected check the master/slave settings
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (E) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au)

faultCodes.meaning: Remote controller control board error (remote controller fault) - inspected unit: remote controller
likelyCauses: Wrong addressing in a grouped system / twin system wired to a non-master indoor unit
checks: Per source: if grouped, check addressing; if twinned, check the controller is wired to the master indoor unit only
Replace the remote controller if the fault persists
faultCodes.source: Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au) / Mitsubishi Mr Slim Error Codes (scribd) - E1 'Remote controller control board error'; becoolrefrigeration.co.uk

faultCodes.meaning: Remote controller control board error (remote controller fault) - inspected unit: remote controller
likelyCauses: Grouping / twin wiring or addressing error
checks: Per source: if grouped, check addressing; if twinned, check the controller is wired to the master indoor only
Replace the remote controller if the fault persists
faultCodes.source: Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au) / Mitsubishi Mr Slim Error Codes (scribd) - E2 'Remote controller control board error'; becoolrefrigeration.co.uk

faultCodes.meaning: Remote controller transmission error (transmitting error) - inspected unit: remote controller
likelyCauses: Remote controller line noise or collision (two main controllers)
Wiring fault on the A/B line
checks: Check the A/B wiring, the main/sub setting of each controller and for noise sources; swap the controller if it persists
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (E) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au)

faultCodes.meaning: Remote controller transmission error (signal receiving error) - inspected unit: indoor
likelyCauses: Remote controller wiring open or poor contact at the indoor board
Indoor board remote controller circuit fault
checks: Check the remote controller wiring at the indoor unit terminal block and connector; check DC voltage on the line; swap controller / indoor board
faultCodes.source: PAR-21MAA Technical Manual, A-control error codes (E) (p.48); Mr.Slim A-control error code list (arma.org.au)

faultCodes.meaning: Remote controller transmission error (transmitting error) - inspected unit: indoor
likelyCauses: Noise or collision on the remote controller line

diagnosticTips: The outdoor unit control board has a 7-segment/LED display and SW1 dip switches for the self-diagnosis (maintenance) monitor: pressures, thermistors, LEV opening, operation history. Use the service handbook 'LED Monitor Display' table for your unit generation.
Codes display on the remote controller together with the unit address and attribute (e.g. OC = outdoor, IC = indoor, BC = BC controller) that raised the fault.

Clearing faults: most check codes clear when the cause is removed and the system is restarted from the remote controller (OFF then ON). Repeated hard faults that lock the outdoor unit (e.g. 1302 high pressure on the second/third occurrence, inverter faults 42xx) require a power cycle at the outdoor unit after repair. Thermistor faults (51xx) put the unit in 3-minute anti-restart on first detection and error stop on the second.

97 codes are transcribed here (City Multi 4-digit codes plus P-series A-control 2-character codes); sub-codes, preliminary codes and inverter detail codes are omitted - the full City Multi Check Code List (1000-series refrigerant/pressure, 2000-series water/drain, 4000-series inverter/power, 5000-series sensors, 6000-series communication, 7000-series system setting) is in the outdoor unit Service Handbook, Troubleshooting [1] Check Code List, and the summary PDF at mitsubishielectric.com.sg (CityMultiErrorCode.pdf).

Where codes appear: City Multi 4-digit check codes display on the wired remote controller (PAR-2x/3x MA controllers, ME controllers) together with the address and attribute of the unit that raised the fault (OC = outdoor, OS = sub outdoor, IC = indoor, BC = BC controller, Lc = Lossnay, RC = remote controller), on the outdoor unit control board 7-segment LED service display, and on centralized controllers (AE-200/EW-50, AG-150). P-series (A-control) 2-character codes (P/E/F/U) display on the wired remote controller; the outdoor board shows the same fault as LED1 (green) / LED2 (red) blink counts.

Self check on the PAR-21MAA / MA remote controllers: press the CHECK button twice in succession to start self-diagnosis; 'CHECK MODE' appears, then after about 10 seconds the unit address and check code alternate at one-second intervals. Each unit stores the latest check code, so it can be recalled even after it was cancelled from the remote. Press CHECK twice within three seconds to exit self check, or press ON/OFF (which also stops the indoor units).

Error history: the self-check results display shows the error history for each unit; the installation manual's 'Error history reset' procedure clears it (when the reset fails, the error contents are displayed again). On City Multi outdoor units, error history with detection time is also saved in service memory and read via the SW1 LED monitor settings in the service handbook.

Outdoor unit maintenance monitor (City Multi): the control board has DIP switch SW1-1 to 1-8; setting SW1 per the 'LED monitor display' table shows pressures (63HS/63LS), thermistor values, LEV openings, compressor frequency, relay outputs and error history on the 7-segment display. Inverter detail codes (e.g. for 4220/4250/5301) are read with specific SW1 combinations given in the handbook (for example SW1 dips 1,2,5,6,8 ON on some generations).

Test run: on P-series outdoor units the test run can be started and finished with DIP switch SW4 on the outdoor control board; on City Multi, test run is started from the remote controller (TEST RUN button / menu) after the addresses are set and the system has been powered 12 hours for crankcase heat. Check code 0900 means a unit (Lossnay) is in test mode, not a fault.

Communication faults: for 66xx codes measure the M-NET DC voltage at TB3 (indoor/outdoor) and TB7 (centralized control) on the outdoor unit and confirm the transmission booster is powered; never wire or change polarity on the transmission line with power on (causes 6602). For 683x codes check the MA remote controller A/B line, the number of controllers/indoor units in the group and the main/sub setting; indoor board LED2 shows whether the MA line is powered.

Mr. Slim P-series with an M-NET interface reports A-control faults as City Multi 4-digit codes (for example U1 -> 1302, U2 -> 1102, UF -> 4100, UP -> 4210, P5 -> 2502, E6 -> 6607-type communication codes); the MrSlimerrorCode.pdf table lists both forms side by side.
