ledPatterns.pattern: P-series (A-control) outdoor controller board: LED1 (green) and LED2 (red) blinking counts indicate the type of abnormality; detailed codes require the optional A-Control Service Tool PAC-SK52ST on connector CNM
ledPatterns.meaning: The blinking patterns of both LED1 and LED2 indicate the abnormality type; the same fault is shown as a U/E/F/P check code on the wired remote controller. Read the count of blinks on each LED and look it up in the 'Display function of inspection for outdoor unit' table for that outdoor model
checks: Read the LED1/LED2 pattern with the outdoor unit powered and the fault active; cross-check the check code on the remote controller (CHECK mode)
Consult the outdoor unit service manual table for the model (patterns differ slightly by generation)

ledPatterns.pattern: P-series outdoor: LED1 3 blinks + LED2 1 blink
ledPatterns.meaning: Abnormality of shell thermistor (TH32) / discharging temperature (TH4), or abnormal high pressure (high-pressure switch 63H worked) - corresponds to remote controller codes U2 / U1
checks: Check TH4/TH32 resistance and placement; check head pressure, outdoor fan, coil and stop valves; check 63H switch and connector

ledPatterns.pattern: P-series outdoor: LED1 1 blink + LED2 2 blinks
ledPatterns.meaning: Open connector(s) on the outdoor board (protection device connector 63L/49C open) - corresponds to remote controller codes F3 / F4 / F9
checks: Check the 63L, 49C and 63H connectors and device continuity on the outdoor controller board

ledPatterns.pattern: P-series outdoor (pump-down / refrigerant collection): LED1 off, LED2 lit
checks: Close the liquid stop valve first, run pump-down per the service manual, then close the gas valve when LED2 lights

ledPatterns.pattern: P-series outdoor (pump-down / refrigerant collection): LED1 lit, LED2 off and the outdoor unit stopped
ledPatterns.meaning: Refrigerant collection was not properly performed
checks: Repeat the refrigerant collection procedure; check that the stop valves and SW settings match the service manual sequence

ledPatterns.pattern: City Multi outdoor control board: 7-segment / LED error display lit with all SW1 dip switches OFF
ledPatterns.meaning: The current check code (and error source address/attribute) is shown on the outdoor unit LED service display; other SW1 settings select maintenance-monitor items (pressures, thermistors, LEV opening, error history)
checks: Set all SW1 switches OFF to read the check code; use the 'LED monitor display' table in the service handbook to set SW1 for detail codes, sensor values and history

If the LED error display is lit with all control-board connectors except CNDE disconnected, the fault is on the board itself; if it appears when a connector is reconnected, the fault is in that wiring/component

ledPatterns.pattern: City Multi indoor unit board: LED1 lit / LED2 lit
ledPatterns.meaning: LED1 indicates the indoor unit main power is on; LED2 indicates the MA remote controller line is powered
checks: LED1 off: check indoor unit power supply and fuse; LED2 off with an MA controller connected: check the A/B remote controller line for a short and the indoor board (relates to 6831-6834 faults)

controls.name: LG Multi V VRF error codes (CH codes)
controls.description: CHxx codes shown on the indoor unit / wired controller display and on the outdoor unit 7-segment display; CH01-CH19 indoor, CH21-CH59 outdoor/inverter and communication, CH100+ HR units and newer generations. Coverage is partial: transcribed from search excerpts of the LG Multi V 5 service manual per-code pages, the Multi V (III) manual self-diagnosis list, the LG wall-mounted inverter service manual, LG Global video-guide titles, LG Help Library pages and LG's CH150 technical bulletin, corroborated by rapidhvacparts / acerrorcode / ARMA lists. Not transcribed (seen only as TOC entries): CH12, CH48, CH49, CH54, CH59, CH77, CH79, CH113-115, CH173, CH180, CH182, CH1xx HR-unit sensor codes beyond 201, and codes CH243-CH272 referenced by LG's guide index. The existing pack entry already carried CH01, CH05, CH21 and CH53 (secondary sources); this sidecar re-sources them to the Multi V 5 / wall-mount service manuals and keeps the meanings consistent. Wall-mount SM excerpt for CH25 in one search summary quoted garbled voltage limits ('over 373 V or below 776 V'); the numeric thresholds were not carried into the meaning. Severity mapping: 'shutdown' = codes the manuals describe as stopping the compressor/system (Level 1-3), 'warning' = sensor open/short codes that stop the affected unit but are field-repairable, 'info' = CH07 mode conflict which only blocks the conflicting indoor unit.

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor unit air (return air) temperature sensor open or short - 'Air temperature sensor of indoor unit - open or short'; Multi V5 table: 'Indoor unit air temperature sensor disconnected or shorted'.
likelyCauses: Sensor connector unplugged or poorly seated on the indoor PCB
checks: Manual: check wiring and the connection on the indoor unit PCB, then check the thermistor
Field: measure sensor resistance unplugged against the 10 kohm-class thermistor table; measure sensor voltage plugged in
Replace sensor, then indoor PCB if the input still reads open/short
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V manual (686189) p.60 self-diagnosis code list; LG Multi V5 SM p.126 Table 68; LG USA Help Library CH01

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error: outdoor unit to indoor unit - 'failing to receive outdoor unit signal in indoor unit PCB'.
likelyCauses: Communication wiring open, reversed polarity, or not shielded/grounded
Outdoor unit not powered or main PCB fault
Auto addressing not completed after installation
checks: Manual (wall-mount SM p.57 / Multi V5 SM): check the communication cable between outdoor unit PCB and indoor unit PCB; reconnect
Verify outdoor unit power and that auto addressing was run
Field: DC communication voltage on the indoor/outdoor communication terminals; shield grounded at one end only
Level 2 (communications) response - activates after 10 failed attempts to communicate
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM Table 68 / Error No. 05; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.57 'Troubleshooting CH05, CH53'; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH05, 53, 237'

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit inverter compressor IPM fault - 'Inv. PCB IPM fault (fault or drive fault)' - DC peak / over-current detected by the intelligent power module.
likelyCauses: Compressor winding short or locked rotor
Water or moisture on the IPM
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.144): check the inverter PCB assembly and compressor IPM heat sink; replace the inverter PCB assembly if faulty
Wall-mount SM: check insulation from water at the IPM part and the IPM circuit
Field: compressor winding resistance U-V/V-W/W-U balanced and megohm to ground; DC bus voltage
Always apply heat transfer paste to a new inverter PCB heat sink
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.144 'Error No. 21'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM pp.59-61 (CH21 IPM fault); LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH21, 29'

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error between master indoor and outdoor units, detected at the outdoor unit - 'failing to receive indoor unit signal at the outdoor unit'.
likelyCauses: Communication cable between outdoor unit external PCB and indoor unit PCB open/reversed
Communication cable between cycle (main) PCB and outdoor external PCB
Indoor unit count mismatch after auto addressing
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.168): check the communication cable between outdoor unit external PCB and indoor unit PCB, reconnect; check the cable between cycle PCB and outdoor unit PCB; check cable and installation
Level 2 (communications) response after 10 failed attempts
Verify the number of indoor units shown on the outdoor 7-segment display vs. installed
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.168 'Error No. 53'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.57 'Troubleshooting CH05, CH53'; LG Help Library 'Checking code CH53'

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor unit inlet pipe temperature sensor open or short - 'Inlet pipe temperature sensor of indoor unit - open or short'; Multi V5: 'Indoor unit inlet pipe temperature sensor disconnected or shorted'.
likelyCauses: Connector not seated on the indoor PCB
checks: Manual: check the connection on the indoor unit PCB
Field: sensor resistance vs. temperature table; check the sensor is clipped to the pipe
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V manual (686189) p.60; LG Multi V5 SM p.126 Table 68

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error: wired remote controller to indoor unit - 'failing to receive wired remote controller signal in indoor unit PCB'.
likelyCauses: Remote controller cable open, shorted or miswired (polarity)
checks: Check remote controller cable continuity and terminal connections at both ends
Swap in a known-good wired remote controller
Check DC voltage on the remote controller terminals; replace indoor PCB if no signal
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.137 'Error No. 03'; LG Multi V manual (686189) p.60; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH03'

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor unit outlet pipe temperature sensor open or short - 'Outlet pipe temperature sensor of indoor unit - open or short'.
checks: Check connector seating on the indoor PCB
Sensor resistance vs. table; replace sensor then PCB
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM Table 68 / Error No. 06; LG USA Help Library CH06

faultCodes.meaning: Different operation mode - 'Indoor unit is set in different cool/heat operation mode' from the other indoor units on the same (heat pump) outdoor unit.
likelyCauses: One indoor unit calling for heating while the system is in cooling (or vice versa) on a heat-pump (non-heat-recovery) outdoor unit
Mode priority / master indoor unit setting
checks: Set all indoor units to the same mode, or set a master unit / mode lock on the central controller
On heat recovery systems check the HR unit valve addressing
faultCodes.source: LG USA Help Library 'Guide to Error Codes' (CH07: units set to different operating modes); acerrorcode.com / orionair LG Multi fault code sheet ('C7 Different operation mode')

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor unit EEPROM error - 'serial number marked on EEPROM of the indoor unit is 0 or FFFFFF' (EEPROM check-sum mismatch).
likelyCauses: EEPROM not inserted / inserted backwards after PCB replacement
checks: Check EEPROM seating and orientation on the indoor PCB
Replace EEPROM with the correct part for the model, else replace the PCB
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM Error No. 09; acerrorcode.com ('C9 EEPROM check sum')

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor unit fan motor poor operation / BLDC fan motor lock - 'fan motor connector disconnected or failure of indoor fan motor lock'.
likelyCauses: BLDC fan motor locked or failed
checks: Check fan motor connector at the indoor PCB
Spin the blower by hand; check motor windings and the feedback (Hall) signal
Replace motor, then PCB
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM Error No. 10; acerrorcode.com ('CA BLDC fan motor lock'); LG USA Help Library CH10

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter board input over-current (RMS) - 'current excess'; light-commercial: 'Max. C/T' (CT2 maximum current).
likelyCauses: Internal CT / diode / resistor circuit fault on the inverter PCB
checks: Wall-mount SM: check the power source, fan operation, current, install condition, and the internal circuit (C/T, diode, resistor)
Field: measure supply voltage under load and compressor amps against nameplate
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM Table 69 'Error No. 22' (Inverter board input over current RMS); LG wall-mounted inverter SM pp.59-61 'CH21, CH22 Max. C/T'

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter compressor DC link low voltage - 'DC charging not performed after starting' (low DC voltage sensed at the outdoor inverter).
likelyCauses: Input power loss or low voltage
Charging relay / rectifier fault on the inverter PCB
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.148): check DC link connections
Wall-mount SM p.60: check TAB1 connected; DC link voltage below 300 V when not operating means fault
Field: measure DC bus voltage during start; check reactor and power wiring
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.148 'Error No. 23' (Table 79); LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.60 'CH23 DC Link Low voltage'

faultCodes.meaning: High pressure switch open - 'Press S/W open' (mechanical high pressure switch tripped).
checks: Wall-mount SM p.60: verify 'CN_PRESS' connection, check the install condition for overload, check the SVC valve open, check for refrigerant leakage
Multi V5 SM p.149: replace the high pressure switch if it has failed open
Field: compare gauge high-side pressure with the switch set point before condemning the switch
faultCodes.source: LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.60 'CH24 Press S/W Open'; LG Multi V5 SM p.149 'Error No. 24'

faultCodes.meaning: Input voltage high/low - 'Outdoor unit input voltage is out of range' (abnormal supply voltage).
likelyCauses: Inverter PCB voltage sensing (Trans1, bridge diode) fault
checks: Wall-mount SM p.60: check the power source and components (Trans1, B/Diode, diode, resistance)
Multi V5 SM p.150: verify supply, then replace inverter PCB assembly if sensing is wrong
Field: measure L-L voltage at the unit under load and at idle
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.150 'Error No. 25'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.60 'CH25 Input voltage'

faultCodes.meaning: DC compressor position detection error - inverter compressor starting failure.
likelyCauses: Compressor windings open/unbalanced or compressor seized
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.151): check U-V, V-W, W-U winding resistance for the compressor model (e.g. JQC048MA/MB table) and check the inverter compressor PCB assembly and IPM
Wall-mount SM p.62: 'CH26 DC Compressor Position'
Field: megohm the compressor; try a restart after correcting wiring
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.151 'Error No. 26'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.62 'Troubleshooting CH26, CH27'; LG USA Help Library CH26

faultCodes.meaning: PSC fault - 'CH27 PSC Fault' (power-factor/PFC over-voltage protection circuit fault; third-party lists describe it as over-voltage / high DC voltage).
likelyCauses: PFC circuit / reactor fault on the inverter PCB
checks: Wall-mount SM p.62: follow the CH26/CH27 troubleshooting flow - check power source, then the inverter PCB
Field: check supply voltage and DC bus voltage; replace inverter PCB if it persists
faultCodes.source: LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.62 'Troubleshooting CH26, CH27'; hvacreport.co.uk / becoolairconditioning (over-voltage description)

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter compressor over-current - 'Inverter compressor input current is >30A'.
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.153): check if the inverter compressor PCB assembly and IPM are correct; apply heat transfer paste to a new inverter PCB heat sink
Field: clamp compressor amps at start and run; check operating pressures and charge
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.153 'Error No. 29'; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH21, 29'

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter compressor 1 discharge temperature high - 'system/compressor shuts off because of high discharge temperature' (discharge pipe >115 C / 239 F for 10 s, or compressor dome 105 C / 221 F for 10 s).
likelyCauses: Defective inverter compressor discharge pipe temperature sensor
checks: Manual flow (Multi V5 SM p.155): check refrigerant level, discharge temperature sensor resistance, EEV operation in heating mode, and piping blockages
Field: measure actual discharge temperature and superheat; verify liquid injection
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.155 'Error Nos. 32 and 33'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.63 'CH32 D-pipe (Inverter) temp high'; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH32, 33'

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter compressor 2 (or constant-speed compressor) discharge temperature high - same trip limits as CH32.
checks: Same as CH32 for compressor 2's discharge sensor, EEV and injection valve
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.155 'Error Nos. 32 and 33'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.63 'CH33 D-pipe (Constant) temp high'

faultCodes.meaning: High pressure - 'excessive rise of discharge pressure' in the outdoor unit (high pressure sensor over limit); LG split help: safety relay powered the unit down because of abnormal pressure in the sealed system.
likelyCauses: Defective outdoor PCB or pressure sensor
checks: Manual (LG Multi V SM): replace the corresponding pressure sensor or EEV, open the SVC valve, replace the PCB, check/replace fan parts, clean the indoor filter / outdoor heat exchanger, adjust refrigerant amount
Field: compare the high pressure sensor reading (LGMV) with a gauge; check condenser airflow and ambient
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V Service Manual (ManualsLib 2125885) high-pressure troubleshooting; LG Multi V5 SM Table 69 'Error No. 34'; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH34'; LG Egypt help 'CH34, CH35'

faultCodes.meaning: Low pressure - excessive drop of low (suction) pressure detected by the low pressure sensor.
likelyCauses: Strainer or EEV clogged (frost/ice at the strainer)
Indoor airflow loss in cooling, outdoor coil blocked in heating
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.157): if the temperature difference across the strainer is large enough to frost, check for clogs; replace the low pressure sensor if it reads wrong
Field: compare low pressure sensor value (LGMV) with a gauge; check charge by subcooling / superheat
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.157 'Error No. 35'; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH35'; acerrorcode.com Multi V list

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter compressor CT (current transformer) sensor fault - 'CT Sensor Fault' for the outdoor unit inverter compressor.
likelyCauses: Inverter PCB CT sensing circuit fault
checks: Check input voltage; check the inverter PCB CT sensing circuit (wall-mount SM p.63)
Replace inverter PCB assembly if the CT circuit is faulty
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM 'Error No. 40'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.63 'Troubleshooting CH32, CH33, CH40 (CT sensor)'

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter compressor discharge pipe temperature sensor (TH3) open or short - 'defective compressor discharge pipe sensor that is either opened or shorted'.
likelyCauses: Poor solder / connector on the PCB
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.160): insert the sensor connector to the PCB correctly; replace the sensor; replace the corresponding outdoor unit PCB
Check resistance of the discharge temperature sensor against the standard values by temperature (wall-mount SM p.64: estimate resistance unplugged and voltage plugged)
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.160 'Error Nos. 41 and 47'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.64 'CH41 D-pipe sensor (Inverter)'

faultCodes.meaning: Low pressure sensor open or short.
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.161): confirm the sensor is connected to the PCB correctly; measure the V DC supply and signal to GND; replace the corresponding pressure sensor
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.161 'Error Nos. 42 and 43'; acerrorcode.com ('CH42 low pressure sensor fault')

faultCodes.meaning: High pressure sensor open or short.
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.161): confirm the sensor is connected to the PCB correctly; measure V DC and signal to GND; replace the pressure sensor
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.161 'Error Nos. 42 and 43'; LG USA Help Library CH43

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit air (ambient) temperature sensor open or short.
checks: Wall-mount SM p.64: estimate the resistance of the sensor unplugged and the voltage plugged in
Multi V5 SM p.162: replace the sensor (resistance varies with temperature)
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.162 'Error Nos. 44, 45, 46, 49, 153, and 154'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.64 'CH44 Air sensor'; LG USA Help Library CH44

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit condenser (heat exchanger) pipe temperature sensor open or short.
checks: Same sensor resistance / voltage checks as CH44; replace sensor then PCB
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.162; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.64 'CH45 Condenser Pipe sensor'; LG USA Help Library CH45

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit suction pipe temperature sensor open or short.
checks: Same sensor resistance / voltage checks as CH44; replace sensor then PCB
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.162; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.64 'CH46 Suction Pipe sensor'; LG USA Help Library CH46

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor 2 / constant-speed compressor discharge pipe temperature sensor open or short - 'D-pipe sensor (Constant)'.
checks: Same procedure as CH41 on the second compressor's discharge sensor
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.160 'Error Nos. 41 and 47'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.64 'CH47 D-pipe sensor (Constant)'

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit three-phase power missing - one or more of the R(L1), S(L2), T(L3) input power line connections is missing.
likelyCauses: Inverter PCB input current sensor error
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.163): check R~S / S~T / T~R phase voltage is 208-230 V +/-10%; rewire and/or replace if errors are found; replace inverter PCB assembly
Note: reverse / open phase is a different code (CH54) - swapping two phases cures reversed rotation
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.163 'Error No. 50'; acerrorcode.com LG Multi V list (CH50 3-phase power missing)

faultCodes.meaning: Over capacity - 'Combination ratio is out of range' (connected indoor capacity exceeds the outdoor unit's allowed combination ratio).
likelyCauses: Too many / too large indoor units connected
Indoor unit capacity DIP/EEPROM settings wrong
checks: Total the connected indoor capacities against the outdoor unit's allowed combination ratio
Check indoor unit capacity settings and rerun auto addressing
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.164 'Error No. 51(1)'; LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.65 'CH51 Over capacity'

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error between outdoor unit inverter PCB and main PCB (main PCB fails to receive the inverter PCB signal).
checks: Check the communication cable between inverter PCB and main PCB; check inverter PCB power LEDs
Replace inverter PCB, then main PCB
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.166 'Error No. 52 - Communication error between outdoor unit ...' (title truncated in the excerpt seen); rapidhvacparts LG CH guide

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error: main PCB to inverter PCB - 'failing to receive the signal from the main PCB at the inverter PCB of the outdoor unit'.
likelyCauses: Inverter PCB or main PCB defective
Communication cables run with power cables (noise)
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.170): check the communication cable; replace inverter PCB; replace main PCB
Run communication cables separately from power cables
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.170 'Error No. 57'; LG Multi V Installation Manual (ManualsLib 1191304) error list

likelyCauses: EEPROM missing, wrong, or inserted in the wrong direction after PCB replacement
checks: Manual: check EEPROM checksum and direction, EEPROM insertion condition, power and installation, inverter PCB screw connections, 15 V DC input on the inverter PCB
Replace EEPROM, else the inverter PCB assembly
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM 'Error No. 60' (inverter PCB EEPROM); LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.65 'CH60 EEPROM Check sum'

faultCodes.meaning: Condenser pipe (outdoor heat exchanger) temperature high - 'Condenser pipe sensor temp high'; third-party: outdoor unit overheating in cooling / indoor coil overheating in heating.
likelyCauses: Blocked or dirty outdoor coil, poor ventilation around the outdoor unit
checks: Wall-mount SM p.66 CH61 flow: check outdoor coil/fan and the condenser pipe sensor
Field: measure condensing temperature vs. ambient; clean coil, verify fan speed
faultCodes.source: LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.66 'Troubleshooting CH61, CH62'; hvacreport.co.uk / becoolairconditioning LG code lists

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter PCB heat sink temperature high - 'Heat sink sensor temp high' (system turns off).
likelyCauses: Heat sink dirty or airflow over it blocked
Missing heat transfer paste / loose PCB mounting
checks: Wall-mount SM p.66 CH62 flow: check heat sink cleanliness, fan operation and the heat sink sensor
Multi V5 SM: if the inverter PCB is replaced, replace the heat sink and apply heat-transfer paste
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM 'Error No. 62' (Inverter PCB heatsink temperature high); LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.66 'CH62 Heat sink sensor temp high'

faultCodes.meaning: Inverter heat sink temperature sensor open or short.
likelyCauses: Heat sink thermistor open/short or poorly soldered
checks: Wall-mount SM p.64: estimate the resistance of the heat sink sensor unplugged and its voltage plugged in
Replace sensor / inverter PCB
faultCodes.source: LG wall-mounted inverter SM p.64 'CH65 Heat sink sensor'; LG Multi V5 SM 'Error No. 65'

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor fan lock - outdoor (BLDC) fan motor locked or not rotating.
likelyCauses: Fan motor windings or Hall sensor
checks: Manual: check the fan condition (rotates freely), fan motor wiring and connector
Multi V5 SM p.115 'Checking the outdoor unit fan motor' and p.121 'Checking the fan IPM'
faultCodes.source: LG Universal System Air Conditioner SM (ManualsLib 766627) p.105 'CH67 Outdoor fan lock'; acerrorcode.com ('CH67 outdoor fan motor / BLDC fan error')

faultCodes.meaning: Fan CT sensor error - 'Fan CT sensor' (Master: 751).
likelyCauses: Fan PCB IPM / current sensing circuit
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.176): check if the fan PCB IPM is correct; replace fan PCB assembly
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.176 'Error No. 75'

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit main PCB EEPROM error.
likelyCauses: EEPROM not inserted / wrong EEPROM after main PCB replacement
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.180): recheck power and installation; insert the EEPROM; reset after checking the EEPROM assembly; replace with the correct EEPROM
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.180 'Error No. 86'

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error between outdoor units - 'failure to receive a Slave unit signal at the main PCB of the Master outdoor unit'.
likelyCauses: Inter-unit communication cable (A/B) open or reversed
Ground wire not bonded to chassis
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.182): connect communication cable, connect power wiring, connect GND wire with chassis, connect A and B properly
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.182 'Error No. 104'

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error between inverter PCB and fan PCB - 'failure to receive a fan signal at the main PCB' (Master: 1051).
likelyCauses: Inverter compressor PCB to fan PCB connection not correct
Outdoor unit inverter compressor PCB and/or fan PCB defective
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.185): check the communication cable between inverter compressor PCB and fan PCB; verify power to the inverter 1 / inverter 2 terminals on the main PCB; replace the inverter PCB assembly
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.185 'Error No. 105'

faultCodes.meaning: Fan PCB IPM fault - 'PCB IPM error' on the outdoor fan drive.
likelyCauses: Fan motor locked or wiring fault
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.187): recheck power and installation; fan motor wire connections; check whether the outdoor fan motor assembly is locking up; replace fan PCB assembly
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.187 'Error No. 106'

faultCodes.meaning: Fan PCB DC link low voltage - inverter PCB to fan PCB DC link defective / disconnected.
likelyCauses: DC link wiring between inverter PCB and fan PCB disconnected
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.189): measure DC link voltage; replace fan PCB assembly
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.189 'Error No. 107'

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error between the master outdoor unit main PCB and the external (communication) PCB.
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.191): check communication between main PCB and external PCB; run communication cables separately from power cables
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.191 'Error No. 145'

faultCodes.meaning: Liquid compression prevention (low suction superheat) - 'an error to prevent liquid compression which can induce serious compressor failure': suction superheat below 3 C (4.8 F) for 5 minutes while the outdoor unit is in cooling; shuts down and auto-restarts, escalating on repeat.
likelyCauses: Flood-back / bypass at an indoor unit: indoor unit OFF with EEV open passes liquid without superheat
Subcooler EEV in the heat recovery box or the ODU sub-cooler EEV stuck open
Indoor EEV or coil sensor fault
checks: LG TB: find the indoor unit whose outlet pipe is cold while off (EEV not closing); check HR-box and ODU subcooler EEVs
Field: monitor suction superheat in LGMV; isolate indoor units to find the bypassing one
faultCodes.source: LG Technical Bulletin 'Multi V CH150 error guide' (Scribd copy); LG Multi V5 SM p.192 'Error No. 150'

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor unit operation mode / reversing-valve error - 'the reversing valve has not switched correctly between heating and cooling'.
likelyCauses: 4-way valve coil open, disconnected or wrong coil
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.193): reconnect the four-way valve / change or re-insert the four-way valve coil; replace outdoor unit PCB; replace the four-way valve
Field: check coil continuity, listen for the valve shifting, compare discharge and suction temperatures before/after mode change
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.193 'Error No. 151'; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH151'; airnexus / rapidhvacparts LG code lists

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit upper heat exchanger temperature sensor error (open/short) - note: the Multi V 5 SM summary table reportedly labels 153 as an inverter heat sink temperature sensor error while the detail page describes a liquid pipe (condenser) sensor; confirm on the specific unit.
checks: Multi V5 SM p.162: replace the sensor (resistance varies with temperature)
Check both the upper heat exchanger / liquid pipe sensor and the inverter heat sink sensor for open/short before replacing
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.162 'Error Nos. 44, 45, 46, 49, 153, and 154' (grouped sensor page); rapidhvacparts LG CH guide; acerrorcode.com

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor unit lower heat exchanger temperature sensor error (open/short).
checks: Multi V5 SM p.162: replace the sensor; verify resistance against the temperature table
faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.162 'Error Nos. 44, 45, 46, 49, 153, and 154' (grouped sensor page); rapidhvacparts LG CH guide; acerrorcode.com

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor fan PCB heat sink over-temperature (third-party lists describe CH193/CH194 together as 'fan PCB heatsink over-temperature or its sensor error'; which number is the temperature trip vs. the sensor fault should be confirmed in the Multi V 5 SM pp.198-199).
likelyCauses: Fan PCB heat sink dirty or airflow blocked
checks: Check heat sink cleanliness and obstructions, fan PCB connections and wiring
Refer to Multi V5 SM Error No. 193 (p.198)
faultCodes.source: rapidhvacparts LG CH guide / airnexus LG VRF fault code list (CH193/194); LG Multi V5 SM TOC 'Error No. 193' p.198

likelyCauses: Heat sink thermistor on the fan PCB open/short
checks: Check the fan PCB heat sink sensor and connections; refer to Multi V5 SM Error No. 194 (p.199)
faultCodes.source: rapidhvacparts LG CH guide / airnexus LG VRF fault code list (CH193/194); LG Multi V5 SM TOC 'Error No. 194' p.199

likelyCauses: Indoor unit piped to an HR-unit valve but not communicating (or vice versa)
Indoor unit EEV / valve not responding during the search
Pipe search run in unsuitable ambient conditions

Compare detected vs. communicating indoor unit counts on the 7-segment display
Level 1 response (outdoor unit shut down); SM p.86 describes the 'level change of error code CH200 (SE14)' setting
faultCodes.source: LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH200, 204'; LG Multi V5 SM p.86 'Level change of error code CH200 (SE14)' and p.105

checks: Check the sensor and connections on the heat recovery unit PCB (code suffix identifies the HR unit number)
faultCodes.source: rapidhvacparts LG CH guide (HR unit codes) - third-party

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error between the outdoor unit and the heat recovery unit - 'the outdoor unit isn't hearing from the heat recovery unit'.
likelyCauses: Communication bus wiring to the HR unit
checks: Check the communication bus wiring and the HR unit PCB power / LEDs; re-run auto addressing
faultCodes.source: LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH200, 204' (title); blog.usro.net / rapidhvacparts descriptions

faultCodes.meaning: Communication error between outdoor unit PCB and indoor unit PCB (indoor unit lost after addressing).

faultCodes.source: LG Multi V5 SM p.206 'Error No. 237'; LG Global video guide 'Error Code CH05, 53, 237'

faultCodes.meaning: Network (RS-485 central control) error - displayed as 2421 Master, 2422 Slave 1, 2423 Slave 2.
likelyCauses: RS-485 communication cable not properly connected
checks: Manual (Multi V5 SM p.208): check the RS-485 cable, verify indoor unit addresses are not repeated, confirm simple central controller settings, recheck power and installation

diagnosticTips: The outdoor unit main PCB has a 7-segment display and function buttons; error codes and operating data cycle on the display. LG's official trouble-shooting video guide covers CH05/CH53/CH237 communication faults.
Clear a communication code by correcting the wiring and cycling power to the outdoor unit; re-run auto addressing if indoor units were added.

56 codes are transcribed here from the Multi V 5 service manual tables 68/69 and per-code pages (corroborated by the Multi V III list and the LG wall-mount inverter SM); HR-unit (CH1xx) and CH2xx codes beyond those listed are in the Multi V service manual and LG's Help Library.

Where codes appear: the indoor unit display window / LED, the wired remote controller display (CHxx), and the outdoor unit main PCB 7-segment LED (SSD). All error codes can also be viewed with the LGMV (LG Monitoring View) service tool / PLGMVW101 Wi-Fi module, which also shows live pressures, temperatures and superheat.

Reading the outdoor SSD: 1st-3rd digits are the error number and the 4th digit is the unit number (1 Master, 2 Slave 1, 3 Slave 2) - ARUM160LTE5 IM p.50; Multi V5 SM p.126 'Error Code Display'. Outdoor unit information cycles in sequence on the main PCB SSD.

Response levels (Multi V5 SM p.125): four levels - Level 4 'notify and keep operating' up to Level 1 'immediate system shutdown, manual restart required'. Non-communication faults start at Level 3 (auto-restart) and escalate to Level 1 on the 10th occurrence; communication faults (CH05/CH53) are Level 2 and activate after 10 failed communication attempts.

Clearing (Multi V 5 SM p.125): after the cause is fixed the error code remains until the master outdoor unit's microprocessor is reset AND operation has resumed for 130 minutes without recurrence; Level 1 faults need a manual power reset at the outdoor unit, Level 4 faults notify and keep operating. Communication codes clear after wiring is fixed and, if indoor units were added or replaced, auto addressing is re-run.

Auto addressing (Multi V5 / ARUM IM p.40): wait 3 minutes after power-up, then press the RED button (SW01C) on the outdoor unit main PCB for 5 seconds; the number of connected indoor units shows on the 7-segment LED for 30 seconds when complete. Heat recovery systems also need auto pipe detection (Multi V5 SM p.105).

Sensor codes (CH01/02/06, CH41-47, CH65, CH153/154): unplug the sensor and measure resistance against the manual's temperature table, then measure the sensor voltage plugged in; replace the sensor before the PCB (wall-mount SM p.64 method).

Inverter codes (CH21/22/23/26/29): check U-V/V-W/W-U compressor winding balance and megohms, the inverter IPM, DC link voltage and connections; always apply heat-transfer paste and use a JIS screwdriver on inverter PCB screws (Multi V5 SM p.209).

Light-commercial LG splits (Multi F, universal/CAC) use the same CH numbering for the common codes (CH01-CH10 indoor, CH21-CH29 inverter, CH32-CH47 sensors/pressure, CH53, CH60-CH67) - the LG General Wall Mounted-Inverter Type service manual is the reference for those; Multi V VRF adds the 3-digit outdoor (CH1xx) and HR/central-control (CH2xx) codes.

faultCodes.meaning: No fault in memory since the last power-up (the fault LED flashes code 1 in Test Mode when no fault is stored)

Condensate sensor probe dirty or shorted
checks: Water level in the drain pan; clear the drain and trap
Continuity of the CO sensor circuit when dry (should be open)
Unit pitch toward the drain
faultCodes.source: ClimateMaster CXM Controls manual 97B0003N12 - condensate overflow fault; ClimateMaster Basic Troubleshooting Information and Guidelines
faultCodes.notes: The numeric code is read in Test Mode (momentarily short the TEST terminals; 20 minutes, timers x15); in normal mode the LED only shows fast flash (lockout).

faultCodes.meaning: Control is in fault retry mode
faultCodes.source: ClimateMaster Basic Troubleshooting Information and Guidelines (files.climatemaster.com)

faultCodes.meaning: Control is in lockout mode
faultCodes.source: ClimateMaster Basic Troubleshooting Information and Guidelines (files.climatemaster.com)

diagnosticTips: Enter Test Mode by momentarily shorting the TEST terminals on the board (Test Mode lasts 20 minutes and speeds all time delays by 15x); the fault LED - and the alarm relay, so the code can be read at the thermostat - then flash the last fault code in memory (code 1 = no fault since power-up). Normal mode LED: steady on = normal, slow flash = fault retry, fast flash = lockout (no numeric code outside Test Mode). Lockout reset: cycle the thermostat (Y) call or the unit power; the last fault is retained in memory and read back in Test Mode.

commonIssues.symptom: Bard wall-mount with ventilation/economizer package: high humidity or no fresh air, damper stuck
likelyCauses: Economizer/ventilation damper actuator failed or linkage disconnected
checks: Command the damper and watch travel
Verify the ventilation package control inputs per the option's instructions
Filter condition; blower amps
sources: Builder inference - no manufacturer source (generic HVAC symptom, not a documented brand bulletin)

commonIssues.symptom: Reznor UD unit heater: venter runs but no ignition, DSI LED 2 flashes (pressure switch did not close)
likelyCauses: Pressure switch not proving: blocked vent/flue, cracked tubing, water in the switch, venter wheel dirty
checks: Draft pressure at the switch tap vs. switch rating
Vent termination, screens, ice
Venter motor current and speed
sources: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM (Form I-UDA) DSI LED table (2 flashes = pressure switch did not close within 30 s of venter start)

commonIssues.symptom: Reznor UD unit heater: ignites then locks out (DSI LED 1 flash = flame not detected / sustained)
likelyCauses: Flame sensor dirty or poor burner ground (weak flame current)
Low gas pressure / propane conversion not done
checks: Flame current in microamps; clean the sensor rod
Inlet/manifold pressure during trial
Ground continuity from the burner to the board
sources: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM (Form I-UDA) DSI LED table (1 flash = system lockout, flame not detected) and ignition-failure causes list

commonIssues.symptom: Modine / UT ignition board: LED 2 flashes (pressure switch closed with no venter call) or 3 flashes (limit open)
likelyCauses: 2 flashes: pressure switch contacts stuck / welded closed, or switch miswired so it reads closed before the venter starts (the board waits indefinitely for it to open)
3 flashes: high limit open - low airflow across the heat exchanger (fan motor / fan relay, dirty propeller, blocked discharge), overfiring
checks: 2 flashes: with no call for heat, ohm across the pressure switch - contacts must be open; check tubing and wiring, replace a welded switch
3 flashes: gas valve is de-energized, blower runs on heat speed and inducer runs; check fan operation, manifold pressure vs. rating plate, reset the limit only after the cause is found
sources: Modine doc 5H79749 'Modine/UT Ignition Control Board Failure Codes' (breeze.modine.com) - 2 flashes pressure switch closed, 3 flashes limit open

commonIssues.symptom: Unit heater: burner cycles on limit (3 flashes), discharge very hot
likelyCauses: Fan motor not running / fan relay or time delay failed
checks: Fan starts within the delay after ignition
Manifold pressure and orifice size vs. rating plate
Inspect heat exchanger for cracks / flame rollout
sources: Reznor UDAP/UDAS IOM DSI LED table (3 flashes = limit or rollout open)
Modine doc 5H79749 'Modine/UT Ignition Control Board Failure Codes' (3 flashes = limit open)

commonIssues.symptom: Mitsubishi City Multi: 6607 / communication errors after a power event or added units
likelyCauses: Transmission line damaged, poor shield grounding, or duplicated addresses

Address switches on the unit named in the code
Shield grounded at one point only
sources: Mitsubishi City Multi error code list - 6607 no ACK

Fan operation and coil condition
Valves open

LEV coil connection and pulse operation
Leak search

commonIssues.symptom: LG Multi V: CH05 / CH53 communication error

Indoor unit not powered / auto addressing not completed

Indoor units recognized on the outdoor display
Re-run auto addressing

Outdoor unit display
Auto addressing

likelyCauses: Condenser fan speed control / Lee-Temp receiver or fan failure (air-cooled)

Condenser fan / speed control operation

likelyCauses: Dirty filters / blocked inlet or outlet
Broken belt or loose blower wheel
Differential pressure switch setting or tubing

Blower motor fuses and overload reset; belts; wheel set screws
Switch tubing and setpoint

commonIssues.symptom: Water-source heat pump: lockout on FP1 water-coil freeze detection (WaterFurnace E5 / ClimateMaster CXM-DXM code 4) in heating
likelyCauses: Freeze setpoint left at 30 F (water) on an antifreeze loop
Low loop flow or cold loop
checks: Board freeze jumper/dip switch setting (15 F for antifreeze)
Loop delta-P and entering water temperature
Charge by subcooling

CO sensor continuity when dry
Unit level/pitch
